study: Smith et al. 2016 — Enhanced Core Reading Instruction (ECRI), grade-1 multitiered, IES Project ECRI (U Oregon)
eval_evidence: Efficacy trial conducted and authored by the ECRI developers/research team (Smith, Nelson, Smolkowski, Baker, Fien — University of Oregon; IES Award R324A090104). Developer-conducted evaluation.
developer_evidence: PD and coaching delivered by 'ECRI expert coaches' (the research team): 'All professional development included teaching demonstrations by ECRI expert coaches and participant practice with coach feedback'; study-group meetings 'facilitated by an ECRI coach'.
cascade_evidence: ECRI expert coaches (developer staff) train and coach the grade-1 teachers and small-group instructors directly; no train-the-trainer intermediary.
counterfactual_evidence: Comparison schools implemented the district-adopted core reading program AND their own multitiered service-delivery model, with Tier-2 students receiving an additional 30 min small-group instruction 'across conditions' — an active alternative, not a true do-nothing BAU.
coaching_evidence: 'comprehensive coaching support through classroom and small-group visits conducted once per month and regular study-group meetings' — recurring (monthly) in-class coaching.
student_dose_evidence: ECRI restructures the content/alignment of Tier-1 and Tier-2 instruction, but the +30 min daily small-group Tier-2 time was given to at-risk students in BOTH conditions ('across conditions'); no added student-facing minutes unique to treatment.
maturity_evidence: Single-cohort efficacy trial; teachers implemented ECRI in the study year (PD began that fall) — first implementation year. No prior-year wave reported.
